industry_closure.commerce: 3 entries, 2 + 1 + 1 = 4, against a printed footing of 4. Closes.
industry_closure.learned_professions_and_engineers: 8 entries, all of them 1, = 8, against a printed footing of 8. Closes.
industry_closure.manufactures_and_trades: 7 entries, 3 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 10, against a printed footing of 15. DOES NOT CLOSE, and the 5 is left open. The column was swept twice over the whole body at 4.5x and carries no eighth entry and no unread cell; the largest single entry is the 3 at line 7, and that 3 is the same glyph as the 3 the navigation-of-canals column carries on the same line, where 3 is the only value that closes. So the shortfall cannot be moved onto line 7 without breaking a column that does close.
industry_closure.navigation_canals_lakes_rivers: 5 entries, 3 + 2 + 10 + 2 + 1 = 18, against a printed footing of 18. Closes.

closure.the_two_residuals: Both columns that fail to close are short by exactly 5 - the TOTAL column reads 193 against 198, and manufactures reads 10 against 15. That the same 5 appears twice is recorded because it is the kind of coincidence a later pass should be able to see; nothing is inferred from it here, and no cause is proposed.
closure.total_column_note: the 31 committed lines sum to 193 against a printed footing of 198. 193 is also what printed 232's own marks give, counted column by column across all 38 of its cells, so two independent leaves agree on 193 and the enumerator's own footing on this one stands 5 above it. That residual is REPORTED, not closed: no line is adjusted and no digit is re-read to make the footing come out. Printed 232's own footings give a third figure, 195, which is 2 above its own marks.

division_note: the printed heading reads '... by the Marshal of the [___] District (or Territory) of Illinois'; the district is written in over the printed line in a hand this exposure does not resolve. Recorded unread rather than inferred from the sheets around it.
familysearch_id_note: none. This leaf is NOT in the project's FamilySearch deposit of 74 images - that the deposit lacks it is the whole finding of T-0543 and T-0736. It was fetched from the Internet Archive's scan of the NARA microfilm and read there; the deposit's read-only rule is untouched, because no image, crop or render from the roll is committed.

footer_as_read.footer_blank_columns_note: mining, agriculture and navigation of the ocean carry no figure at the foot and no ink in the body. The pensioners, deaf/dumb/blind/insane and schools blocks carry neither. Nothing is read as a zero.
footer_as_read.total_glyphs_as_read: 1 9 8 - a slant; a closed loop at the head with a long descender (this leaf's 9, as at line 26, and NOT its 5, which carries a horizontal top bar); and a continuous S crossing itself into two loops (this leaf's 8, as at line 23).
footer_as_read.total_note: SETTLED AT 198. T-0911 read this cell as 195 with 198 as the arguable alternate, from the pairing pass at low magnification. Read here at 6x against the leaf's own 5s (lines 1, 3, 14, 30), its own 9 (line 26) and its own 8 (line 23), the third glyph has no top bar and the second has no bowl under one, so neither is this hand's 5.

form_note: The right (continuation) sheet of the 1840 population schedule: twelve SLAVES columns, TOTAL - number of persons in each family, seven NUMBER OF PERSONS IN EACH FAMILY EMPLOYED IN columns, PENSIONERS FOR REVOLUTIONARY OR MILITARY SERVICES (names and ages), ten DEAF AND DUMB, BLIND, AND INSANE columns and the SCHOOLS, &c. columns. On this leaf the TOTAL column and four of the seven industry columns are written in. The slaves block, the pensioners block, the deaf/dumb/blind/insane block and the schools and illiteracy block carry NO ink and no figure at the foot, and this pass reads them as not written rather than as zeros.

glyph_key.0: a closed oval loop that does not cross itself. It stands second in the TOTAL column's 10 at line 7 and second in the navigation-of-canals 10 at line 12, and nowhere alone.
glyph_key.1: a single slant with no bowl and no top bar. Eight of the leaf's learned-professions entries are this and nothing else.
glyph_key.2: a top curl running down into a flat base.
glyph_key.3: two open bowls facing left, one above the other. It stands twice on line 7 - once in manufactures and once in navigation of canals - and the two are the same glyph.
glyph_key.4: two strokes, a slant and an upright, not joined at the top. It closes the column at line 31 and opens the 14s at lines 12 and 24.
glyph_key.5: a bowl under a horizontal top bar. Lines 1, 3, 14 and 30, and it is NOT the footing's third glyph.
glyph_key.6: an ascending stroke curling into a closed bowl at the foot.
glyph_key.8: a continuous S that crosses itself into two loops. Line 23, and it is the footing's third glyph.
glyph_key.9: a closed loop at the head with a long descender running to the lower left. Line 26, and it is the footing's second glyph.
glyph_key.what: the forms this reading leans on, every one of them taken off this leaf and not off another sheet's hand.

line_index.committed: line n is the n-th entry of the TOTAL column, counted from the heading rule at y 821 down to the last entry above the footing rule. The centres are recorded on each record as total_group_centre_y.
line_index.geometry_note: column bounds are stated at y 800 and carried down the leaf by x(y) = xb + (0.0157 + (xb - 1145) * 7.76e-6) * (y - 800), a shear fitted to three printed rules measured at eight depths. TOTAL is 1145-1321; the seven industry columns are 1321-1390-1456-1510-1588-1656-1728-1789 in printed order.
line_index.why_not_a_uniform_grid: the leaf is warped and the printed rules lean: a vertical rule measured at x 1145 at y 800 stands at x 1167 at y 2200, and the lean grows with x (1789 -> 1818 over the same band), which is a shear and not a rotation - the leaf's two horizontal rules are level to within 4 px across the whole width. A uniform 31-line grid between y 821 and y 2907 gives a pitch of 67.3 px against observed gaps of 49 to 80, so the grid was not used. Each line was taken from its own ink.

lines_note: 31, and every one of them carries a TOTAL. There is no unread line on this leaf and no blank one: the count is the same 31 the left sheet rules and the same 31 T-0911 counted in this column before any cell was read.
method: geometry measured off the image (horizontal rules by a row-darkness profile through the empty slaves block; vertical rules by a local-background-subtracted column profile, and the lean fitted over eight depths); every digit read by a human off magnified, contrast-stretched crops of the measured cells. No digit is read by a tool. tools/read_census_continuation.py was tried first and refuses this leaf - its column locator needs the industry run bracketed by TOTAL and PENSIONERS at the fractions the FamilySearch scans put them, and this is a different digitisation at a different crop - so the geometry was measured directly instead and the tool's rules (local background, not a flat threshold) were kept.

method_calibration.the_independent_check: the TOTAL column was read in full BEFORE it was compared with printed 232, and it reproduces the left sheet's 31 per-line free-person counts position for position, all 31 of 31, with no offset anywhere. The two readings were made five years and two digitisations apart - the left sheet off the FamilySearch deposit in PR #523, this one off the Internet Archive's film scan - and neither was adjusted toward the other.
method_calibration.what: the reading was made against this leaf's own glyph key, and the key was built from the figures the leaf itself cannot be wrong about: the entries that stand alone in a column, and the footings.
method_calibration.what_it_does_not_prove: agreement on the TOTAL column says nothing about the industry columns, which the left sheet does not carry. Those stand on their own footings, and one of them does not close.

pairing_test.how: printed 232's committed per-line free-person counts against this pass's TOTAL column, line for line, and at four neighbouring offsets. The two readings were made independently and neither was adjusted toward the other.
pairing_test.pair_under_test: 33S7-9YYJ-W6, printed page 232, paired to this leaf by T-0911 on the film's order and on n166's names
pairing_test.result: 31 of 31 at offset 0, and no other offset reaches 5 of 30. This is the pairing key T-0543 asked for and could not find inside the deposit: the sequence screen is not merely consistent, it is exact over the whole leaf. The two lines T-0912 was opened on - rows 7 and 11, which the pairing strip left arguable at low magnification - read 10 and 13 here, which is what the left sheet says.
pairing_test.what_this_does_not_settle: the footings still disagree: 193 by both leaves' marks, 195 by printed 232's footings, 198 by this leaf's. The pairing is on the marks, which agree exactly; the footings are the enumerator's arithmetic and are reported as they stand.

printed_page_note: 232 by pairing, not by the stamp. The corner that carries the printed number on this leaf is smudged past reading at this exposure - three glyphs stand there and none resolves - so the number is NOT read here. T-0911 placed the leaf instead by the film's own order (on this roll the left sheet of an opening is filmed before its right: n164, n166, n168 are left and n165, n167, n169 are right) and by n166 carrying printed 232's own 31 heads in order. This pass adds a third strand that is independent of both: all 31 entries of this leaf's TOTAL column reproduce printed 232's own per-line free-person counts, position for position, with no insertion or deletion anywhere in the sequence.
read_pass: The leaf fetched from the Internet Archive and checked against the sha256 the source record carries, then the form's geometry measured off it - the two horizontal rules that bound the body, and the printed vertical rules of the TOTAL column and of the seven industry columns - and every column then read by eye off magnified, contrast-stretched crops of the measured cells. The TOTAL column was read first and alone, band by band, before any comparison with the left sheet was made. The industry columns were read second, each one swept over the WHOLE body at magnification rather than only where an entry was expected, which is what found the blank ones. The pensioners block, the deaf/dumb/blind/insane block and the schools and illiteracy block were swept the same way and carry no ink.

records.total_glyphs_as_read: a slant then a closed oval loop. Read 10. The same pair the left sheet's own count gives for this line.

industry_note.navigation_canals_lakes_rivers: a slant then a CLOSED oval loop, the same pair this leaf writes for 10 in the TOTAL column at line 7. Read 10. The alternates the stroke allows are 18 and 13, and both are refused here for reasons that do not depend on the footing: the loop closes and does not cross itself, which is what separates this leaf's 0 from its 8 (line 23) and from its 3 (line 7, both columns); and 18 would put more persons in one trade than the 14 the same line's TOTAL allows. The column's printed footing closes exactly on 10 and on neither alternate, which is corroboration and was not the reason.

records.total_glyphs_as_read: the two-stroke 4 of this hand written first, then a 1 - read 14.
a continuous S that crosses itself: the leaf's 8. Not the two open left-facing bowls it writes for 3 (lines 20, 21).
the two-stroke 4, standing alone below the last ruled line and above the footing rule.
